$comment: Gate eval set. Each case has hand-collected evidence signals and a reference review (what a careful reviewer concludes from that evidence). `pnpm eval:gates` scores the gate decisions against the labels; `--live` asks the configured model for the review instead. Signals are approximate snapshots, not live data. `ageDays` (days since first published) marks a case as new, where missing discussion and code count only in part. `excerpt` is what the sources say (an abstract, a post), as the production prompt shows it; the young cases are made up and their links illustrative.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: Speculative decoding
legitimacy.summary: A small draft model proposes tokens that the target model verifies in parallel, giving 2-3x faster decoding with identical output distribution.
legitimacy.excerpt: We speed up autoregressive decoding by letting a small draft model propose several tokens that the large target model then scores in one parallel pass; a modified rejection-sampling step accepts or corrects them, so the output distribution is provably the same as the target model's. On T5-XXL we measure 2x-3x faster decoding with identical outputs and no retraining.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: FlashAttention
legitimacy.summary: IO-aware exact attention that tiles the computation to reduce HBM reads, speeding up training and inference.
legitimacy.excerpt: Attention is slow and memory-hungry on long sequences because it reads and writes the full attention matrix to GPU high-bandwidth memory. We propose an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that tiles the computation in on-chip SRAM and recomputes it in the backward pass, cutting HBM accesses. It trains BERT-large 15% faster than the MLPerf 1.1 record and GPT-2 3x faster, and makes longer contexts practical.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: LoRA
legitimacy.summary: Low-rank adapters fine-tune large models by training small rank-decomposition matrices instead of all weights.
legitimacy.excerpt: We freeze the pre-trained weights and inject trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer. For GPT-3 175B this cuts the trainable parameters by 10,000x and GPU memory by 3x, while matching or beating full fine-tuning on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2 and GPT-3, with no added inference latency.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: Task arithmetic in weight space
legitimacy.summary: Task vectors (fine-tuned minus pre-trained weights) can be added or negated to edit model behaviour without retraining.
legitimacy.excerpt: We build task vectors by subtracting a model's pre-trained weights from its weights after fine-tuning on a task. Negating a task vector lowers performance on that task with little change elsewhere, and adding task vectors together improves several tasks at once. We show both across vision and language models.

legitimacy.name: Proof-driven development
legitimacy.summary: Agents write a Verus spec and proof alongside the code, then mutation-check the spec, so generated code is verified for all inputs.
legitimacy.excerpt: With PDD-Kit, coding agents write a Verus specification and proof alongside each function of a full-stack web app, then mutation-test the specification so one too weak to catch seeded bugs is rejected. The kit and the verified example apps are released.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: Property-based testing
legitimacy.summary: Generate many inputs and check invariants (round-trips, idempotence) to find edge cases unit tests miss.
legitimacy.excerpt: Hypothesis generates many inputs from strategies you describe, checks that your properties hold for every one, and shrinks any failure to a minimal example. It is widely used in Python projects and has found bugs in mature libraries that their example-based tests missed.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: DSPy prompt programs
legitimacy.summary: Declarative LM pipelines whose prompts and few-shot examples are compiled against a metric instead of hand-written.
legitimacy.excerpt: DSPy expresses LM pipelines as programs of declarative modules, and a compiler optimizes their prompts and few-shot demonstrations against a metric. Within minutes of compiling, a few lines of DSPy outperform standard few-shot prompting by over 25% with GPT-3.5 and 65% with Llama 2 13B chat on math word problems and multi-hop QA.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: QLoRA
legitimacy.summary: Fine-tune 4-bit quantized models through LoRA adapters, matching 16-bit fine-tuning quality on a single GPU.
legitimacy.excerpt: QLoRA backpropagates through a frozen 4-bit quantized model into LoRA adapters, using a 4-bit NormalFloat data type, double quantization and paged optimizers. It fine-tunes a 65B model on a single 48 GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit fine-tuning performance; our best model reaches 99.3% of ChatGPT's level on the Vicuna benchmark.

legitimacy.summary: A single new preprint with released code reporting 1.5x memory savings; not yet replicated.
legitimacy.excerpt: We propose a KV-cache eviction policy that scores cached tokens by their accumulated attention and always keeps a small window of recent ones. On long-context benchmarks with two open model families it cuts KV-cache memory 1.5x with under 1 point of accuracy loss. Code is released.

legitimacy.label: legit
legitimacy.name: Learned KV-cache eviction (preprint, day 1)
legitimacy.summary: A new preprint from a known lab: a learned eviction policy for the KV cache, with ablations and memory and latency tables in the abstract. No code or discussion yet.
legitimacy.excerpt: We train a lightweight scorer to predict which KV-cache entries future queries will attend to, and evict the lowest-scoring ones. Across four long-context benchmarks and two model families it stays within 0.5 points of full-cache accuracy at 40% of the memory and cuts time to first token by 18%. Ablations separate the learned scorer's contribution from attention-score heuristics.

legitimacy.excerpt: A model proposes unit tests for each function, and a verifier runs them against seeded mutants, keeping only tests that pass on the original code and kill at least one mutant. On Defects4J and a Python benchmark the filtered suites raise mutation scores by 9-14 points over unfiltered generation with a similar number of tests. Code and data are released.
